los.text: Identify the external features of the kidney and explain its function
los.html:
External features
  • Bean-shaped, ~11 cm long, ~150 g
  • Fibrous capsule
  • Convex lateral border
  • Hilum on the medial border (renal vein, artery, pelvis: VAP front to back)
  • Superior and inferior poles.
Coverings(inside → out)Fibrous capsule → perirenal fat → renal (Gerota's) fascia (also encloses the suprarenal) → pararenal fat.
Functions
  • Filter blood and form urine
  • Fluid, electrolyte and acid–base balance
  • Remove waste and drugs
  • Make renin, erythropoietin and activated vitamin D (1α-hydroxylation)
  • Gluconeogenesis.

los.text: Recognise the gross internal features of the kidneys
los.html:
FeatureDetail
CortexOuter layer; glomeruli, convoluted tubules; dips between pyramids as renal columns
Medulla8–18 renal pyramids (loops of Henle, collecting ducts); apex = papilla
Minor calycesCup each papilla
Major calyces2–3, formed by minor calyces
Renal pelvisFunnel → ureter at the pelviureteric junction
Renal sinusFat-filled space round the pelvis and vessels at the hilum

los.text: Draw and label diagrams of coronal and transverse sections of the kidney through the hilum
los.html:
Coronal section through the hilumTransverse section through the hilum
Capsule and outer cortexHilum facing anteromedially
Renal columns between pyramidsVein most anterior, artery in the middle, pelvis most posterior (VAP)
Pyramids with papillae pointing into minor calycesCortex and medulla around the renal sinus
Minor → major calyces → renal pelvis → ureterPsoas medially, quadratus lumborum behind
Segmental arteries and veins in the sinus fatPerirenal fat and renal fascia outside

los.text: List the anterior visceral relationships of both kidneys
los.html:
Right kidney (front)Left kidney (front)
Suprarenal gland (upper pole)Suprarenal gland (upper pole, medial)
Liver (most of the front, via the hepatorenal pouch)Stomach
2nd part of duodenum (medial, at the hilum)Spleen (lateral)
Hepatic flexure of colon (lower pole)Pancreas (tail and body) and splenic vessels
Small intestine (jejunum)Splenic flexure and descending colon, jejunum
  • Behind both: diaphragm (12th rib, pleura), psoas, quadratus lumborum, transversus abdominis; subcostal, iliohypogastric, ilioinguinal nerves.

los.text: List the autonomic nervous and arterial supply, and venous and lymphatic drainage of the kidney
los.html:
SupplyDetail
Arteries
  • Renal arteries from the aorta at L1/2
  • Right is longer and passes behind the IVC → 5 segmental (end) arteries → interlobar → arcuate → interlobular → afferent arterioles.
  • Accessory arteries are common
Veins
  • Renal veins → IVC
  • Left renal vein is longer, crosses in front of the aorta under the SMA (nutcracker), and receives the left gonadal and left suprarenal veins
LymphPara-aortic (lumbar) nodes
SympatheticT10–L1 (lesser and least splanchnic, lumbar splanchnic) via the renal plexus: vasoconstriction, renin release (β1), Na⁺ reabsorption
ParasympatheticVagus (little known function)
PainVisceral afferents with sympathetics → loin to groin pain (T10–L1)

los.text: Describe the adrenal glands' form, relations and functions
los.html:
Right suprarenalLeft suprarenal
ShapePyramidal (triangular)Crescent (semilunar)
PositionUpper pole of the right kidneyMedial border above the hilum
RelationsBehind the IVC (medially) and liver; diaphragm behindBehind the stomach, pancreas and splenic artery; diaphragm behind
  • Inside renal fascia but separate compartment, so it stays when the kidney is removed.
LayerProductFunction
Zona glomerulosaAldosteroneSalt and water
Zona fasciculataCortisolStress, glucose
Zona reticularisAndrogensDHEA ("salt, sugar, sex": GFR)
MedullaAdrenaline, noradrenalineFight or flight

los.text: List the autonomic nervous and arterial supply, and venous and lymphatic drainage of the adrenal glands
los.html:
SupplyDetail
Arteries (3 each side)Superior suprarenal (inferior phrenic), middle suprarenal (aorta), inferior suprarenal (renal artery)
Veins (one each side)Right → IVC directly (very short: risk at adrenalectomy); left → left renal vein
LymphPara-aortic (lumbar) nodes
NervesPreganglionic sympathetic fibres (greater splanchnic, T5–9 roughly) go straight to the medulla with no ganglion: the chromaffin cells act as postganglionic neurons

los.text: Recognise the kidney in normal radiographs and recognise other methods of visualising the kidneys and urinary system
los.html:
• Plain X-ray (KUB): kidney outlines (psoas shadows, perirenal fat); ~90% of stones are radio-opaque; the left kidney is higher.
MethodUse
UltrasoundFirst-line: size, hydronephrosis, cysts, masses; no radiation (pregnancy, children)
CT KUB (non-contrast)Stones
CT urogram (contrast)Haematuria workup: masses, urothelial tumours
IVU (old)Contrast X-ray of calyces, pelvis, ureters
MRIMasses when contrast CT isn't suitable
DMSA scanScarring, split function (children with UTIs)
MAG3 renogramDrainage and obstruction
Micturating cystourethrogramVesicoureteric reflux
Retrograde pyelogramContrast up the ureter at cystoscopy
Renal angiographyRenal artery stenosis

los.text: Identify the muscles of the posterior abdominal wall and explain their actions (psoas major, psoas minor, quadratus lumborum)
los.html:
MuscleAttachmentsActionNerve
Psoas majorT12–L5 bodies, discs, transverse processes → lesser trochanter (with iliacus)Flexes the hip; bends the trunkAnterior rami L1–3
Psoas minor (absent in ~40%)T12–L1 → pectineal line / iliopubic eminenceWeak trunk flexionL1
Quadratus lumborumIliac crest → 12th rib and L1–4 transverse processesLateral flexion of the trunk; fixes the 12th rib in deep breathing; hitches the hipT12–L4
IliacusIliac fossa → lesser trochanterHip flexionFemoral
  • Clinical: psoas abscess (spinal TB, Crohn's) tracks down to the groin below the inguinal ligament
    • psoas sign (pain on hip extension) in retrocaecal appendicitis.

los.text: Describe the origin, course and major branches of the abdominal aorta
los.html:
• Course: enters through the aortic hiatus at T12
    • → down on the vertebral bodies, slightly left of midline
    • → bifurcates at L4 into the common iliac arteries.
TypeBranches (level)
Unpaired, ventral (gut)Coeliac trunk (T12), SMA (L1), IMA (L3)
Paired, lateral (organs)Middle suprarenal (L1), renal (L1/2), gonadal (L2)
Paired, body wallInferior phrenic (T12), lumbar arteries (L1–4)
TerminalCommon iliacs (L4), median sacral
  • AAA: usually infrarenal; screening by ultrasound for men at 65 (NHS AAA screening programme); repair at ≥5.5 cm.

los.text: Construct a labelled diagram of the caval venous system, and identify the important anastomoses
los.html:
• IVC: formed by the common iliac veins at L5 (behind the right common iliac artery)
    • → up on the right of the aorta
    • → through the caval opening of the diaphragm at T8 (in the central tendon)
    • → right atrium.
IVC tributariesNotes
Common iliacsL5
Lumbar veinsLinked by ascending lumbar veins to the azygos system
Right gonadalDirectly (left goes to the left renal vein)
Renal veinsLeft crosses in front of the aorta
Right suprarenalDirectly (left to the left renal vein)
Inferior phrenic
Hepatic veinsJust below the diaphragm
  • Portal vein: drains gut, spleen and pancreas to the liver, not the IVC.
Important anastomosisBetweenClinical
Azygos–caval (ascending lumbar → azygos/hemiazygos)IVC and SVCCollateral route if the IVC is blocked
Portosystemic (oesophagus, rectum, umbilicus, retroperitoneum)Portal and systemicVarices, caput medusae, haemorrhoids in portal hypertension
Superficial epigastric–thoracoepigastricFemoral and axillary veinsDilated abdominal wall veins flowing upwards in IVC obstruction
Vertebral venous plexus (Batson's)Pelvic veins and vertebral veins (valveless)Prostate and breast cancer spread to the spine

los.text: Identify the surface markings of the abdominal aorta and the caval venous system
los.html:
StructureSurface marking
Aortic hiatusT12, midline
Aortic bifurcationL4: about the level of the umbilicus / iliac crests, slightly left of midline
Aortic pulseFelt by deep palpation above and left of the umbilicus; an expansile mass suggests AAA
IVCRight of the midline, from L5 to the 6th right costal cartilage
Caval openingT8, right of midline
Common iliac arteryLine from the aortic bifurcation to the midinguinal point (upper third)

los.text: Describe the location of the kidneys within the abdomen
los.html:
LevelT12–L3; the right kidney is lower (by about half a vertebra) because of the liver.
Hilumat L1 (transpyloric plane), ~5 cm from the midline.
Upper poles are protected by the 11th and 12th ribs; the kidneys move ~2–3 cm with breathing.
Retroperitoneal, in the paravertebral gutters on psoas and quadratus lumborum.
Renal angle(between the 12th rib and erector spinae)Tenderness suggests pyelonephritis.
PalpationBimanual (ballotable) when enlarged; the right lower pole may be felt in thin people.
